newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Stals sees two pct growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Stals sees two pct growth in 97.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals has predicted economic growth of two percent this year, the Johannesburg-based Sunday Times said.
It said he gave the figure in an interview with the paper's Business Times section last week.
"The cyclical growth pattern is clearly working," it quoted him as saying. "After three years of steady growth, 1997 will be a year of consolidation."
Economists predict three percent growth for 1996.
The paper said Stals believed modest growth this year would result in an improvement in the balance of payments and put downward pressure on bank credit extension and inflation.
If so, "there could be some alleviation on the interest rate front", the paper quoted him as saying.
Stals predicted a decline of seven to eight percent in the rand this year, in line with inflation differentials with the country's major trading partners.
The rand fell 29 per cent against the dollar in 1996.
"There is a better understanding of our economic policies and greater political stability," he said.
"There is also a realisation that exchange controls cannot be lifted in a big bang if we don't have the foreign exchange reserves to back the currency," he said.
